transfer_skinning_button.tip: Transfer the rig from a basemesh to a new mesh.
transfer_skinning_button.what: Select the geo group of the closest basemesh, then the new mesh. Copies the skins and attachment groups across.
steps: Shift select the new character geo.
examples: Rig a new crowd character from the male basemesh in one click.
Make ten crowd variants from one rigged basemesh.
Transfer to a new outfit that has the same hierarchy names.
transfer_skinning_button.details: zombie_crowd_copy.name_transfer_hierarchy_skins() copies skins by matching names in the hierarchy, then attachment_groups_copy() rebuilds the attachment groups.

import_male_button.what: Imports the rigged male basemeshes to transfer the rig from.
examples: Import it, then use Transfer Rig on a male character.
Compare your model with the male basemesh proportions.

import_female_button.what: Imports the rigged female basemeshes to transfer the rig from.
examples: Import it, then use Transfer Rig on a female character.
Use it for female crowd agents.

add_combo_button.tip: Add an asset to the combo.
add_combo_button.what: Adds a row for the asset picked above, with its file path, to the combo list.
examples: Add "Zombie_Body" and "Zombie_Hat" to make one combined rig.
Add a hat and a backpack asset to the body combo.
add_combo_button.details: crowds_combo_utils.CrowdsCombo(show).find_asset_path(asset) fills the row; you can edit the path by hand.

create_combo_button.what: Imports every asset in the list and combines them into one rig named after the combined asset.
examples: Fill the list and the combined name, click Create.
Make one rig with body, clothes and props for a crowd agent.
create_combo_button.details: CrowdsCombo(show).create_combo_rig(paths, asset): imports each file and merges them into one rig. Errors if the name or the list is empty.

save_combo.what: Saves the list of asset paths and the combined name to a json file.
examples: Save it to build the same combo again next week.
Save one combo per agent type.
save_combo.details: Writes {"paths": [...], "asset": name} to the json you pick.

load_combo.what: Loads a combo json saved before and fills the list.
examples: Load last week's combo and click Create.
Load the soldier combo and build it on the new body.
load_combo.details: Reads that json, adds one row per path and sets the combined name.

set_combine.tip: Use the picked asset as the combined name.
set_combine.what: Copies the asset picked above into the combined asset field.
examples: Pick the main body asset and click << to name the combo after it.
Name the combo after the body so the files sort together.

ImportSkeleton.what: Imports the crowd skeleton for the type picked in the list (AG, SP, BD...).
examples: Pick AG and click it to get the Atoms skeleton.
Import the toon skeleton (SP) for stylized agents.
ImportSkeleton.details: AG > atoms skeleton; SP and BD > atoms_toon skeleton (crowd_utils).

ReparentSkeleton.tip: Fit the crowd skeleton to the rig.
ReparentSkeleton.what: Matches and parents the crowd skeleton to the rig joints for the type picked in the list.
examples: Import the skeleton, then click it so it follows the rig.
Reparent after building the rig so the skeleton follows it.
ReparentSkeleton.details: match_crowd_to_rig with the joint maps: AG atoms_map > mutant_map, SP atoms_toon_map > mutant_toon_map, BD atoms_toon_map > bd_toon_map.

ReferenceSinning.what: Copies the skinning from the reference crowd geo onto the rig geo.
examples: Use it when the meshes match the reference crowd character.
Copy the skin from the hero agent to a variant.
ReferenceSinning.details: transfer_skin_reference(main_geo_grp="geo", crowds_map="atoms_map", main_joint="Hips"); the reference is kept.

OneToOneSkinning.tip: Copy the skin joint by joint.
OneToOneSkinning.what: Copies the skin weights straight from one joint to its matching joint.
examples: Use it when both skeletons have the same joints.
Move weights from the Mutant joints to the Atoms joints.
OneToOneSkinning.details: transfer_skin_one_to_one(): weights move joint to joint by the map, no closest point guessing.

OffLabelSkinning.tip: Copy the skin by joint labels.
OffLabelSkinning.what: Copies the skin weights by matching joint labels instead of names.
examples: Use it when the joint names differ but the labels are set.
Transfer between skeletons with different naming.
OffLabelSkinning.details: transfer_skin_labels(): matches joints by their side / type labels. Run Helpers > Label All Joints first if labels are missing.

create_game_joints_button.what: Makes the game skeleton from the biped rig, and moves the skin to it if the check is on.
steps: Turn on the skin check to move the skin too.
examples: Turn on the skin check, click it, export the game skeleton.
Make the export skeleton for Unreal.
create_game_joints_button.details: games_utils.create_biped_game_joints(do_skins): a clean *_Skl skeleton driven by the rig; with do_skins the skins move from the bind joints to it.

simplify_btn.what: Turns the hero template skeleton into the simple game skeleton (fewer joints).
examples: Use it for background characters that need fewer bones.
Cut the joint count for mobile games.
simplify_btn.details: convert_hero_template_skl_to_simple_skl(): merges extra joints (rolls, tweaks) into their parents, weights included.

examples: Import it, then Setup Face Skeleton.
Add a face skeleton to a game character.

setup_face_skeleton_button.what: Connects the game face skeleton to the face rig.
examples: Click it after Import Face Skeleton.
Drive the game face joints from the face ctrls.

clasic_linear_skin_button.tip: Set the skins to Classic Linear.
clasic_linear_skin_button.what: Switches the skinClusters to Classic Linear, the method game engines use.
examples: Click it before exporting to the engine so it looks the same there.
Match what the engine will show before exporting.
clasic_linear_skin_button.details: skinningMethod = Classic Linear on every skinCluster.

set_max_inf_to_four_button.what: Sets every skin to at most 4 joints per vertex, as most engines need.
examples: Click it before the FBX export.
Fix "too many influences" errors on FBX import.
set_max_inf_to_four_button.details: set_max_inf(4): prunes and normalizes every skin to 4 influences per vertex.

delete_constriants_button.tip: Delete the constraints in the skeleton.
delete_constriants_button.what: Removes the constraints inside the main skeleton, leaving clean joints for export.
examples: Click it on a copy of the rig, right before exporting.
Clean a baked skeleton copy before export.
delete_constriants_button.details: Deletes the constraints under the main game skeleton. The skeleton stops following the rig: do it on an export copy.

SegmentScaleOn_Bttn.what: Turns on segment scale compensate on the skeleton joints.
examples: Turn it on to go back to the Maya default.
Turn it back on after the export test.
SegmentScaleOn_Bttn.details: segmentScaleCompensate 1 on the game skeleton joints.

SegmentScaleOff_Bttn.what: Turns off segment scale compensate on the skeleton joints, as game engines expect.
examples: Turn it off so scaled joints look the same in the engine.
Check the arm scale looks the same as in the engine.
SegmentScaleOff_Bttn.details: segmentScaleCompensate 0 on the game skeleton joints (Unreal / Unity do not have it).

turn_off_inherits_transform_on_selected_.tip: Inherits Transform off on the selected joints.
turn_off_inherits_transform_on_selected_.what: Turns off Inherits Transform on the selected joints.
examples: Select the joints that double transform and click it.
Stop a joint double scaling with its parent.
turn_off_inherits_transform_on_selected_.details: setAttr inheritsTransform 0 on the selected joints.

turn_on_inherits_transform_on_selected_b.tip: Inherits Transform on, on the selected joints.
turn_on_inherits_transform_on_selected_b.what: Turns Inherits Transform back on for the selected joints.
examples: Undo the OFF button on some joints.
Restore the default on joints after a test.
turn_on_inherits_transform_on_selected_b.details: setAttr inheritsTransform 1 on the selected joints.

AnimateFaceRig.tip: Animate the face for the export.
AnimateFaceRig.what: Keys the face ctrls through the poses in the SDK map, to feed the DemBones process.
examples: Click it, then Export Alembic, FBX, DemBones.
Animate the face to bake DemBones for a crowd agent.
AnimateFaceRig.details: Reads crowd_utils/SDKMap.json (SDKMap_BD.json on BD rigs with Geo_Grp / Control_Grp) and keys the face ctrls through those poses, one per frame.

LoadFaceGeo.tip: Use the selected geo as the face geo.
LoadFaceGeo.what: Puts the selected geometry in the face geo field.
examples: Select the head mesh and click <<.
Load the face mesh of the agent before exporting.

ExportData.tip: Export Alembic, FBX and run DemBones.
ExportData.what: Exports the animated face geo and runs DemBones to make joints that copy the face shapes.
steps: Fill the face geo field with <<.
Click it and wait for DemBones.
examples: Animate the face first, then click it and wait.
Export once per agent face variant.
ExportData.details: face crowds generate_output(geo): FBX + Alembic of the animated face, then runs DemBones to solve joints and weights that copy the shapes.

ImportData.what: Brings back the joints and geo made by DemBones.
examples: Click it once the export finished.
Import to check the solved joints follow the shapes.
ImportData.details: import_dembones_output(): brings back the solved joints and the skinned geo.

ConnectFaceRig.tip: Connect the DemBones joints to the crowd rig.
ConnectFaceRig.what: Drives the DemBones joints from the crowd rig ctrls, hides the extra ctrls and cleans the skin.
examples: Last step: click it and test the face ctrls.
Connect so the crowd agent face uses the rig ctrls.
ConnectFaceRig.details: connect_ctrls_2_dembones(): drives the DemBones joints from the crowd rig ctrls, hides unused ctrls and cleans the skinCluster.
